newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD finance expert says cabinet in panic.
newsitem.headline: German SPD finance expert says cabinet in panic.

text.p: The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Thursday criticised Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government for exaggerating tax revenues and understating expenditures for too long.

"Kohl's chaos cabinet is now in a panic," said Karl Diller, the SPD's parliamentary spokesman for financial affairs. "Finance Chaos Minister Waigel is now lying in the budget hole he has been denying since November 1996."

Diller said that the SPD had warned Waigel last November when the budget was passed that there would be huge holes. He said Waigel had deliberately overestimated tax revenues and underestimated expenditures by billions of marks.

"What Waigel was calling taboo just recently is now no longer holy at all," Diller said, referring to the possibility the government may sell its stake in Telekom or revalue Bundesbank gold to plug budget holes.
"He doesn't seem to care at all about...the confidence of small shareholders who were counting on the government to keep its promise and not sell its shares before the year 2000," Diller said.

"After selling off the government's silver, the coalition now wants to get its hands on the Bundesbank's gold," he added. "A year ago Waigel said selling the gold to finance the budget would hurt market confidence in German financial policies."

He added: "The coalition's gold deal is an admission that German financial policies have gone to the dogs under the Kohl government. Kohl's chaos cabinet has now hit bottom." -- Bonn newsroom, 49 228 260 97160
